segments.narration: Six-foot waves smashed Japan out of a completely calm night. In January 1700, ocean surges battered villages—without any earthquake felt beforehand.
For centuries, samurai logs called it the orphan tsunami. No volcano had erupted, and zero earthquakes were felt in Asia.
Then geologists found ghost forests across the Pacific in North America. What killed an entire cedar forest at that exact same hour?
Saltwater flooded them when the Cascadia fault violently snapped. A magnitude 9.0 megathrust earthquake dropped the American coastline six feet.
Dendrochronology dated the tree deaths to the 1699 growing season, whereas Japanese tsunami records and wave reconstructions pinpointed the exact date and time to around 9:00 PM on January 26, 1700.

verdicts.claim: An orphan tsunami struck the coast of Japan in January 1700 without a locally felt earthquake.
verdicts.note: The article confirms that a tsunami hit the coast of Japan in January 1700 and that no one in Japan had felt an earthquake before the waves struck.

verdicts.claim: Historical Japanese samurai records documented the mysterious 1700 tsunami as having no known local seismic origin.
verdicts.note: The article confirms that historical Japanese records documented the tsunami occurring without a locally felt earthquake, but it does not mention samurai.

verdicts.claim: Geologists discovered dead cedar ghost forests along the Pacific Northwest coast of North America.
verdicts.note: The article mentions studies of ghost forests of red cedar trees in Oregon and Washington along the Pacific Northwest coast.

verdicts.claim: A magnitude 9.0 megathrust earthquake on the Cascadia subduction zone lowered the North American coastline.
verdicts.note: The article describes an estimated magnitude 8.7–9.2 megathrust earthquake on the Cascadia subduction zone that lowered coastal forests into the tidal zone.

verdicts.claim: Dendrochronology of ghost forest tree rings dated the Cascadia earthquake to around 9 PM on January 26, 1700.
verdicts.note: Tree-ring studies (dendrochronology) only dated the outermost growth rings of the ghost forests to 1699. The specific date and time of 9:00 PM on January 26, 1700 was inferred from Japanese tsunami records combined with ocean wave reconstructions.
verdicts.correction: Dendrochronology dated the tree deaths to the 1699 growing season, whereas Japanese tsunami records and wave reconstructions pinpointed the exact date and time to around 9:00 PM on January 26, 1700.
